images.after: Split every payment the day it arrives
images.title: Where each client payment goes
images.alt: Flow of a freelancer's client payment: a share to tax savings, a share to the buffer, the rest in business checking, then one monthly transfer to personal.
images.caption: The exact split matters less than doing it every single time a payment lands.
images.note: Ask your accountant for the tax share. There's no standard set.

items.label: Client pays
items.text: The money lands in business checking

items.label: Tax savings
items.text: Move a share first. It already belongs to the IRS and your state

items.label: Buffer
items.text: Move a share that covers a slow month or a late client

items.label: Business checking
items.text: The rest covers expenses and your own pay

items.label: Personal account
items.text: One fixed transfer a month, on the same date

images.after: Set aside tax money every time you get paid
images.title: Two federal tax rules for freelancers
images.alt: Cards summarizing US self-employment tax at 15.3 percent and quarterly estimated payments with due dates of April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15.
images.caption: No employer withholds for you, so tax money has to come out of each payment.
images.note: US federal rules only. Your state may have its own estimated payments.

items.title: Self-employment tax
items.text: Generally owed on net earnings of $400 or more; covers Social Security, Medicare

items.title: The 15.3% rate
items.text: 12.4% Social Security plus 2.9% Medicare, generally on 92.35% of net earnings

items.title: Quarterly estimates
items.text: Generally required if you expect to owe $1,000 or more when you file

items.title: Four due dates
items.text: April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15 of the following year

images.after: How to handle clients who pay late
images.title: Prevent late payment before work starts
images.alt: Five steps to prevent late client payments: take a deposit, put terms in writing, invoice immediately, follow up on a schedule, stop work when overdue.
images.caption: Most late payment is preventable before the work starts.

items.title: Take a deposit
items.text: Ask for part of the fee upfront and tie the rest to milestones

items.title: Put terms in writing
items.text: Due date, how to pay and what happens if late, in the contract and invoice

items.title: Invoice immediately
items.text: Send the invoice the day the milestone is done

items.title: Follow up on a schedule
items.text: A reminder before the due date, another the day after, a call a week later

items.title: Stop work when overdue
items.text: Say so in the contract, so pausing is a known term, not a confrontation
